To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stochastic hybrid minimum principle for hybrid stochastic systems with both autonomous switching and controlled switching and jumps is established and that the stochastic hybrid Hamiltonian and adjoints are discontinuous at the switching times and satisfy a set of boundary conditions at switching manifolds.
the Stochastic Hybrid Maximum Principle holds for a class of stochastic hybrid control systems that are driven by a diffusion process and have both autonomous and controlled switching events.

the Stochastic Minimum Principle holds for a class of stochastic hybrid control systems; it includes both autonomous and controlled switching; the state space dimension may change at switching times; the state space has a non-trivial structure, and the state jumps are accompanied by changes of the state space dimension; the state jumps are not necessarily Markovian; the switching manifolds are hard constraints for the state trajectories; and the switching costs are included in the objective functional.
In summary, our research is concerned with
stochastic control of systems with both autonomous switching and jumps and control-driven jumps and switching.
the development of a general theory of stochastic hybrid systems, with applications to optimal control of stochastic hybrid systems.
a class of stochastic hybrid control systems with both autonomous switching and jumps and controlled state jumps and switches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results presented in this thesis provide a rigorous mathematical basis for the study of stochastic hybrid systems and their application in stochastic hybrid control systems.
the theory of stochastic hybrid systems, as it is presented in this paper, provides a solid basis for a wide range of applications in stochastic optimal control and stochastic differential games.
the results of this paper provide an important step forward in the development of the theory of optimal control of stochastic hybrid systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Minimum Principle is a very general tool for the analysis of optimal control problems associated with stochastic hybrid systems and that the Minimum Principle can be applied to a wide range of stochastic hybrid control problems.
we have extended the stochastic minimum principle to a new class of stochastic hybrid control problems.
we have developed a general stochastic hybrid minimum principle for a class of stochastic hybrid optimal control systems which are more general than those considered in the literature so far.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Stochastic Hybrid Maximum Principle is a natural extension of the Stochastic Maximum Principle to a class of stochastic hybrid control systems.
the Stochastic Hybrid Maximum Principle can be used to derive the Stochastic Hybrid Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation for this class of hybrid stochastic control problems.
the stochastic hybrid minimum principle is a powerful tool for analyzing the optimal control of hybrid systems.
